the catalytic combustion of CO/propylene/propane mixture could be predicted by the kinetic models for the combustion of individual components.

the kinetic model for the catalytic combustion of carbon monoxide is a first-order reversible Eley-Rideal mechanism, and the kinetic model for propylene is a first-order Eley-Rideal reaction mechanism.

the Eley-Rideal mechanism is the most appropriate for the catalytic combustion of carbon monoxide and propylene, while the Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism is the most reasonable for propane combustion.
